story: At 11:17 on a humid, hazy Tuesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is elbow-deep in his parade cart at home when Donna arrives eager to recruit him for pickleball before lunch. Gary cheerfully agrees to spare a few minutes while stepping carefully around the wire on his floor. Meanwhile, Hal and Rosa are both heading out onto Magnolia Loop with the same quiet determination, though neither has said where they're going.
events: Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Donna just walked up while I'm halfway through wiring the cart. I've been dodging her pickleball question and she's been generous with her spare paddle, so I should be friendly rather than just keep my head down. The wiring is the main job today, but the harness is run and the speaker's test-fit, so a short word with her costs nothing. I'll greet her warmly and be upfront that I'm busy with the cart. I'm not going to mention the Architectural Review thing to anyone unprompted. That nagging guilt about the permits is a problem for later, once the cart's actually running.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna! Come on in, mind the wire on the floor. I'm knee-deep in the parade cart, but I can spare a few minutes. What brings you by?

donna.thought_process: I'm at Gary's house with the spare paddle packed. He hasn't answered my earlier invite, and I shouldn't repeat it word for word. Better to be direct and cheerful: I'm here, paddle in hand, and I want to lock him in as my doubles partner. Keep it short and give him an easy yes: thirty minutes, coffee on me, and a court booked for two hours max.

parameters.content: Gary, I came to you since you didn't come to me. Spare paddle's in the bag, the court's open till noon, and I'll have you back before lunch. Grab your sneakers, you're my doubles partner now.

hal.thought_process: I've already scanned the street twice and my notebook has the dated entries on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos. No one is nearby, and more observation won't change the facts. The evidence is in hand, so the next step toward my goal is carrying it to the architectural review committee at Town Hall. Rules exist so neighbors don't have to argue, but I'm still uneasy about Gary's garage wiring, so I'll document it factually and fairly. Time to stop watching and start filing.

parameters.content: Heading out with my notes to file the cart modification and flamingo reports with the review committee.

rosa.thought_process: I've already picked an evening with no shift and checked the pantry and fridge, and I wrote the grocery list for four. The list is done, so poking around the kitchen again would be spinning my wheels. The dinner won't happen if I sit here, and I only invited Hal so far. Gary and Donna still need to hear about it from me directly. Nobody is nearby, so the next step is to get out to Magnolia Loop, find my neighbors and pin down a date they can all make. The groceries can wait until the date is set.

parameters.content: Grocery list is done, so I'm heading out to find Gary and Donna, invite them in person, and lock in an evening that works for all three.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
